section_1.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Scaling Dimensions
section_1.content: Establish the foundation by visualizing the growth of a hyper-cube (L-norm) versus the containment of a sphere as dimensions increase. Define the hypersphere equation: x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ² = R².
section_1.example: Visualizing a 1D line segment, 2D circle, and 3D sphere to establish the pattern of enclosure.

section_2.title: The Paradox of Volume: Where did it go?
section_2.content: Explain the counter-intuitive behavior where the volume of a unit hypersphere approaches zero as the dimension n approaches infinity, even though the radius is 1.
section_2.example: A 'Robot Scout' trying to capture a volume of space; as it gains more dimensions, it finds its 'net' captures almost nothing of the surrounding hyper-cube.

section_3.title: The Crusty Shell: Concentration of Mass
section_3.content: Explain that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a hypersphere is concentrated in a thin 'crust' near the surface. The interior becomes essentially empty.
section_3.example: An 'Orange-Slice' analogy: imagine peeling an orange where the peel is the vast majority of the volume, and the fruit inside is mathematically negligible.

section_4.title: Visualization Techniques: Projection and Slicing
section_4.content: Introduce how we represent these objects via 2D projections (Shadows) and cross-sectional slices. Discuss how 'distance' behaves differently in high-dimensional space.
section_4.example: Using a 3D light-box to project a 4D hypersphere onto a 2D screen, creating a pulsing, morphing geometric shadow.

section_5.title: Real-world Application: Data Science
section_5.content: Connect high-dimensional spheres to the 'Curse of Dimensionality' in Machine Learning, where data points become equidistant and spheres are used to define boundary classifications.
section_5.example: An AI facial recognition system classifying 'faces' as points on a high-dimensional hypersphere surface to distinguish between different individuals.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(f"- {line}", font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
